prompt.en: In the simple free-space model, a wanted station is north and a noise source is east. Which horizontal dipole wire route puts the wanted station broadside and the noise source off an end?

feedback.en: The north station is broadside to an east-west wire, while the east noise source lies along an end direction.
This reverses the intended use of the pattern: north is near an end direction and east is broadside.
The north station and east noise source both lie about 45 degrees from this wire axis, rather than at the broadside and end directions.
This diagonal also places both directions between the maximum and null; its end points northwest and southeast, not east.

explanation.en: Use the pattern for both signal pickup and noise rejection. Real ground and surroundings can alter this ideal comparison.

prompt.en: For a square full-wave loop, a learner calculates 306 / f and uses that value for every side. What is the right correction?

text.en: Use 300 / f on each side because loops use the free-space formula.

feedback.en: That changes the estimate slightly but leaves the perimeter-versus-side mistake. It would still use about four wavelengths of wire.
Dividing frequency by four makes the result four times the perimeter, rather than finding a quarter of it.

text.en: Divide 306 / f by two for each side, as for dipole legs.

feedback.en: A square has four sides, unlike the two legs of a dipole. Halving would still use twice the planned perimeter.

text.en: Treat 306 / f as the full perimeter and divide by four for each side.

feedback.en: The loop estimate gives total wire around the square. Four equal sides share that perimeter.

explanation.en: Choose the antenna formula, then divide the total according to the geometry.

prompt.en: An end-fed wire setup produces transmit audio distortion that changes when station leads move. Which path deserves investigation?

text.en: Unwanted RF returning on station wiring because matching or counterpoise control is poor.

feedback.en: Lead-sensitive symptoms suggest RF in the operating area. Investigate return paths and common-mode control.

text.en: Only speech-processing compression, because all transmitted distortion begins in audio settings.

feedback.en: Audio settings can cause distortion, but lead-sensitive changes point to RF coupling that also needs investigation.

text.en: Ordinary linear feedline attenuation, treating every reduction in RF power as audio distortion.

feedback.en: Linear attenuation reduces signal level rather than creating the described audio distortion. Lead-sensitive changes call for an RF coupling investigation.

text.en: A guaranteed harmonic, because every lead-sensitive fault is an integer multiple.

feedback.en: Lead sensitivity does not establish a harmonic relationship. Measure before selecting that diagnosis.

explanation.en: Use the physical clue to trace RF coupling rather than assigning a transmitter-emission label without evidence.
